+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal, and that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this
+# Orca build expects. Also its launchers: node mode, signals forwarded into
+# the sandbox (so `orca-ide serve` stops cleanly), Ctrl-C, and a GUI that
+# outlives `orca-ide open`.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
+# against the host's libraries outside the FHS env. The skills are stubs
+# that tell the agent to run `orca-ide skills get <name>`, so a skill without a
+# working CLI is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a commit separately
+# from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other silently installs
+# guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes in
+# resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+# /etc/hostname is what CI writes to say which host it is; Orca's sandbox does
+# not bind it in, so fall back to uname -n there.
+HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || uname -n).config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
+}
+drv=$(pkg_attr orca-cli drvPath) || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+want_version=$(pkg_attr orca-cli version) && [ -n "$want_version" ] \
+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }
+CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
+gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+GUI=$(nix-store --realise "$gui_drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $CLI and $GUI"
+
+# The skills' own rule: outside an Orca terminal, on Linux, the CLI is
+# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
+# must not also claim `orca-ide` -- in the profile it would shadow one of them.
+for b in orca orca-ide; do
+  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
+done
+if [ -x "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ] && [ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca-ide" ]; then
+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide to the CLI"
+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi
+
+# Run from an Orca terminal, this test is already inside the GUI's FHS env, so
+# a bare wrapper exec'ing the Electron binary would pass every case below.
+# Hold the launcher itself to being a bwrap one.

+  pass "the CLI runs in its own bwrap FHS env"
+else fail "CLI launcher" "$cli_bwrap does not exec bwrap"; fi
+

+# Electron in the CLI's env, with no wayland flag, fonts or nixGL.

+# Exactly the profile's GUI: the unwrapped one has an orca-ide-app too, minus nixGL.

+  pass "orca open launches the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI"
+else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}', want $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"; fi
+

+# argv; Node rejects --ozone-platform, so the wrapper must leave it off there.

+  pass "orca-ide-app runs in node mode (serve's runtime probe)"
+else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "${out:-$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")}"; fi

+# signals the outermost pid, and bwrap forwards nothing: without a forwarding
+# launcher a TERM kills bwrap and the process inside keeps the profile lock.
+# Node mode stands in for the GUI here: same launcher, and it can report what
+# it saw. Each payload exits on its own after 20s, so a regression cannot leak
+# it. Started via env --default-signal, as Node's spawn would: a background
+# job of this non-interactive shell would otherwise begin with SIGINT ignored,
+# which bash then cannot trap. And under setsid: its own session, so no
+# terminal however the suite is run, and its own group ($w), so a signal can
+# go to the whole group. (setsid execs in place: $w is the launcher.)

+      process.on(s, () => { console.log("got-" + s); process.exit(0); });
+    console.log("ready"); setTimeout(() => process.exit(3), 20000);' >"$1" 2>&1 &
+  w=$!
+  for _ in $(seq 150); do grep -q ready "$1" && break; sleep 0.2; done

+# or a KillMode=control-group stop reaches the whole group, and a bwrap that
+# died of one would SIGKILL the payload (--die-with-parent) before its own
+# handler finished.
+bw=$(cat /proc/"$w"/task/*/children 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')
+ign=$(awk '/^SigIgn:/ {print $2}' /proc/"$bw"/status 2>/dev/null)

+if [ -n "$ign" ] && [ $(( 0x$ign & mask )) -eq "$mask" ]; then pass "the launcher's bwrap ignores HUP, INT and TERM"

+  pass "TERM to the GUI launcher reaches the process in the sandbox"
+else fail "TERM forwarding" "rc=$rc, saw: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$T/term")"; fi
+
+# The serve supervisor forwards SIGINT to its child too; off a terminal the

+  pass "INT to the GUI launcher (no terminal) reaches the process in the sandbox"
+else fail "INT forwarding" "rc=$rc, saw: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$T/int")"; fi

+        'let n = 0; process.on("SIGINT", () => { n++; setTimeout(() => {'
+        ' console.log("ints=" + n); process.exit(0); }, 1500); });'
+        ' console.log("ready"); setTimeout(() => process.exit(3), 20000);'])

+def read_until(s, secs):
+    global buf
+    t = time.time()
+    while s not in buf and time.time() - t < secs:
+        try:
+            if select.select([fd], [], [], 0.5)[0]: buf += os.read(fd, 1024)
+        except OSError: break
+read_until(b"ready", 30); os.write(fd, b"\x03"); read_until(b"ints=", 10)
+m = re.findall(r"ints=\d+", buf.decode(errors="replace"))  # the echoed ^C precedes it
+print(m[-1] if m else "none", os.waitpid(pid, 0)[1])
+EOF
+)
+  if [ "$got" = "ints=1 0" ]; then pass "Ctrl-C on a pty reaches the payload once, and it exits cleanly"
+  else fail "Ctrl-C" "got $got (want ints=1, status 0)"; fi
+else
+  echo "skip Ctrl-C on a pty: no python3"
+fi

+# A background job's stdin is /dev/null unless the launcher says otherwise,
+# and the CLI reads stdin.
+got=$(echo stdin-ok | ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e 'process.stdin.pipe(process.stdout)' 2>&1)

+else fail "stdin" "got '$got'"; fi

+# `orca-ide serve`), wrapping its own bwrap.
+if grep -q 'forward-signals' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" 2>/dev/null \
+   && grep -q '\.orca-ide-bwrap' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide"; then
+  pass "the CLI forwards signals into its sandbox too"
+else fail "CLI launcher" "$CLI/bin/orca-ide is not the forwarding launcher"; fi

+# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached and returns. The launcher shell
+# outlives that parent, and the GUI's bwrap is the launcher's child, so
+# --die-with-parent stays on: it is what takes the GUI down if the launcher
+# is SIGKILLed (the serve supervisor's last resort) instead of orphaning it.

+if grep -q '/bin/bwrap' "$gui_launcher" 2>/dev/null && grep -q -- '--die-with-parent' "$gui_launcher"; then

307	+for b in orca orca-ide; do
308	+  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
309	+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
310	+done
311	+if [ -x "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ] && [ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca-ide" ]; then
312	+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide to the CLI"
313	+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi
314	+
315	+# Run from an Orca terminal, this test is already inside the GUI's FHS env, so
316	+# a bare wrapper exec'ing the Electron binary would pass every case below.
317	+# Hold the launcher itself to being a bwrap one.
318	+cli_bwrap=$(readlink -f "$CLI/bin/.orca-ide-bwrap")
319	+if grep -qE '^exec "\$\{cmd\[@\]\}"|/bin/bwrap' "$cli_bwrap"; then
320	+  pass "the CLI runs in its own bwrap FHS env"
321	+else fail "CLI launcher" "$cli_bwrap does not exec bwrap"; fi
322	+
323	+# `orca open` spawns the app; without ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE that is the raw
324	+# Electron in the CLI's env, with no wayland flag, fonts or nixGL.
325	+app=$(grep -o -- '--setenv ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE [^ ]*' "$cli_bwrap" | awk '{print $3}')
326	+# Exactly the profile's GUI: the unwrapped one has an orca-ide-app too, minus nixGL.
327	+if [ "$app" = "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ]; then
328	+  pass "orca open launches the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI"
329	+else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}', want $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"; fi
330	+
331	+# `orca-ide serve` probes that same executable in node mode, with a script as
332	+# argv; Node rejects --ozone-platform, so the wrapper must leave it off there.
333	+# Print, not exit status: if the env var were lost on the way, this would be a
334	+# GUI launch, which a running Orca's single-instance lock answers with 0.
335	+out=$(ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -p '"node-ok"' 2>"$T/node-err")
336	+if [ "$out" = node-ok ]; then
337	+  pass "orca-ide-app runs in node mode (serve's runtime probe)"
338	+else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "${out:-$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")}"; fi
339	+
340	+# Stopping `orca-ide serve` (systemctl, its own supervisor, a plain kill)
341	+# signals the outermost pid, and bwrap forwards nothing: without a forwarding
342	+# launcher a TERM kills bwrap and the process inside keeps the profile lock.
343	+# Node mode stands in for the GUI here: same launcher, and it can report what
344	+# it saw. Each payload exits on its own after 20s, so a regression cannot leak
345	+# it. Started via env --default-signal, as Node's spawn would: a background
346	+# job of this non-interactive shell would otherwise begin with SIGINT ignored,
347	+# which bash then cannot trap. And under setsid: its own session, so no
348	+# terminal however the suite is run, and its own group ($w), so a signal can
349	+# go to the whole group. (setsid execs in place: $w is the launcher.)
350	+payload() { # payload <out-file>: node-mode GUI launch reporting TERM/INT/HUP
351	+  ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 env --default-signal=INT setsid "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e '
352	+    for (const s of ["SIGTERM", "SIGINT", "SIGHUP"])
353	+      process.on(s, () => { console.log("got-" + s); process.exit(0); });
354	+    console.log("ready"); setTimeout(() => process.exit(3), 20000);' >"$1" 2>&1 &
355	+  w=$!
356	+  for _ in $(seq 150); do grep -q ready "$1" && break; sleep 0.2; done
357	+}
358	+
359	+payload "$T/term"
360	+# While it runs: bwrap ignores HUP, INT and TERM. Ctrl-C, a terminal hangup
361	+# or a KillMode=control-group stop reaches the whole group, and a bwrap that
362	+# died of one would SIGKILL the payload (--die-with-parent) before its own
363	+# handler finished.
364	+bw=$(cat /proc/"$w"/task/*/children 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')
365	+ign=$(awk '/^SigIgn:/ {print $2}' /proc/"$bw"/status 2>/dev/null)
366	+mask=$(( (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) | (1 << 14) ))  # HUP, INT, TERM
367	+if [ -n "$ign" ] && [ $(( 0x$ign & mask )) -eq "$mask" ]; then pass "the launcher's bwrap ignores HUP, INT and TERM"
368	+else fail "bwrap signals" "bwrap ($bw) SigIgn=${ign:-unreadable}"; fi
369	+kill -TERM "$w" 2>/dev/null; wait "$w"; rc=$?
370	+if grep -q got-SIGTERM "$T/term" && [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
371	+  pass "TERM to the GUI launcher reaches the process in the sandbox"
372	+else fail "TERM forwarding" "rc=$rc, saw: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$T/term")"; fi
373	+
374	+# The serve supervisor forwards SIGINT to its child too; off a terminal the
375	+# launcher must pass it on, not swallow it.
376	+payload "$T/int"
377	+kill -INT "$w" 2>/dev/null; wait "$w"; rc=$?
378	+if grep -q got-SIGINT "$T/int" && [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
379	+  pass "INT to the GUI launcher (no terminal) reaches the process in the sandbox"
380	+else fail "INT forwarding" "rc=$rc, saw: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$T/int")"; fi
381	+
382	+# TERM to the whole group (a terminal's HUP, a control-group stop) reaches
383	+# bwrap too; it must survive to let the payload's handler run.
384	+payload "$T/group"
385	+kill -TERM -- -"$w" 2>/dev/null; wait "$w"; rc=$?
386	+if grep -q got-SIGTERM "$T/group" && [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
387	+  pass "TERM to the launcher's whole group lets the payload handle it"
388	+else fail "group TERM" "rc=$rc, saw: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$T/group")"; fi
389	+
390	+# Only HUP/INT/TERM deaths are re-raised: a plain exit above 128 is a status,
391	+# and re-raising 148 (TSTP) would stop the launcher instead of exiting it.
392	+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e 'process.exit(148)' >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
393	+if [ "$rc" -eq 148 ]; then pass "a plain exit 148 comes back as 148"
394	+else fail "exit status" "exit 148 came back as $rc"; fi
395	+
396	+# Ctrl-C itself, on a real pty: the payload sees exactly one SIGINT and gets
397	+# to handle it. Needs python3 for the pty, which CI's tool shell lacks.
398	+if command -v python3 >/dev/null; then
399	+  got=$(timeout 60 python3 -I - "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" <<'EOF'
400	+import os, pty, re, select, sys, time
401	+pid, fd = pty.fork()
402	+if pid == 0:
403	+    os.environ["ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE"] = "1"
404	+    os.execv(sys.argv[1], [sys.argv[1], "-e",
405	+        'let n = 0; process.on("SIGINT", () => { n++; setTimeout(() => {'
406	+        ' console.log("ints=" + n); process.exit(0); }, 1500); });'
407	+        ' console.log("ready"); setTimeout(() => process.exit(3), 20000);'])
408	+buf = b""
409	+def read_until(s, secs):
410	+    global buf
411	+    t = time.time()
412	+    while s not in buf and time.time() - t < secs:
413	+        try:
414	+            if select.select([fd], [], [], 0.5)[0]: buf += os.read(fd, 1024)
415	+        except OSError: break
416	+read_until(b"ready", 30); os.write(fd, b"\x03"); read_until(b"ints=", 10)
417	+m = re.findall(r"ints=\d+", buf.decode(errors="replace"))  # the echoed ^C precedes it
418	+print(m[-1] if m else "none", os.waitpid(pid, 0)[1])
419	+EOF
420	+)
421	+  if [ "$got" = "ints=1 0" ]; then pass "Ctrl-C on a pty reaches the payload once, and it exits cleanly"
422	+  else fail "Ctrl-C" "got $got (want ints=1, status 0)"; fi
423	+else
424	+  echo "skip Ctrl-C on a pty: no python3"
425	+fi
426	+
427	+# A background job's stdin is /dev/null unless the launcher says otherwise,
428	+# and the CLI reads stdin.
429	+got=$(echo stdin-ok | ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e 'process.stdin.pipe(process.stdout)' 2>&1)
430	+if [ "$got" = stdin-ok ]; then pass "the launcher passes stdin through"
431	+else fail "stdin" "got '$got'"; fi
432	+
433	+# The CLI uses the same launcher (it is what systemctl stops for a service
434	+# `orca-ide serve`), wrapping its own bwrap.
435	+if grep -q 'forward-signals' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" 2>/dev/null \
436	+   && grep -q '\.orca-ide-bwrap' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide"; then
437	+  pass "the CLI forwards signals into its sandbox too"
438	+else fail "CLI launcher" "$CLI/bin/orca-ide is not the forwarding launcher"; fi
439	+
440	+# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached and returns. The launcher shell
441	+# outlives that parent, and the GUI's bwrap is the launcher's child, so
442	+# --die-with-parent stays on: it is what takes the GUI down if the launcher
443	+# is SIGKILLed (the serve supervisor's last resort) instead of orphaning it.
444	+gui_launcher=$(readlink -f "$GUI/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped")
445	+if grep -q '/bin/bwrap' "$gui_launcher" 2>/dev/null && grep -q -- '--die-with-parent' "$gui_launcher"; then
446	+  pass "the GUI's bwrap dies with its launcher"
447	+else fail "GUI launcher" "$gui_launcher lacks --die-with-parent (or is missing)"; fi
448	+# And the payload outlives a parent that spawns it detached and exits.
449	+bash -c 'ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 setsid "$1" -e "
450	+  setTimeout(() => require(\"fs\").writeFileSync(process.argv[1], \"alive\"), 3000);
451	+  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 4000);" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 &' _ "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" "$T/alive"
452	+for _ in $(seq 75); do [ -s "$T/alive" ] && break; sleep 0.2; done
453	+if [ -s "$T/alive" ]; then pass "the GUI outlives the parent that spawned it (orca-ide open)"
454	+else fail "GUI lifetime" "payload died with its spawning parent"; fi
455	+
456	+# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's runScript
457	+# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
458	+contents=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
459	+  [ -f "$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json" ] && echo "$p"; done | head -1)
460	+[ -n "$contents" ] || { echo "no extracted AppImage in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
461	+manifest="$contents/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"
462	+
463	+# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
464	+clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
465	+outside() { env $(compgen -e | grep '^ORCA_' | sed 's/^/-u /') PATH="$clean_path" "$@"; }
466	+
467	+got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
468	+if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qwF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
469	+else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi
470	+
471	+# What every skill stub runs, under both names the stubs choose between.
472	+for b in orca-ide orca; do
473	+  got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/$b" skills get orca-cli 2>&1)
474	+  if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '^# Orca CLI'; then pass "$b skills get orca-cli prints the guide outside Orca"
475	+  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
476	+done
477	+
478	+# The rev is pinned by hand next to the version; the app knows its own.
479	+rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')
480	+if [ -n "$rev" ] && grep -aqF "sourceCommit:\`$rev\`" "$contents/resources/app.asar"; then
481	+  pass "skills rev ${rev:0:8} is this build's sourceCommit"
482	+else fail "skills rev" "'${rev:-unparsed}' is not the sourceCommit in app.asar"; fi
483	+
484	+for s in $SKILLS; do
485	+  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
486	+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }
487	+  # The source is a subpath of a fetch; realise the fetch's derivation itself.
488	+  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
489	+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)
490	+  nix-store --realise "$srcdrv" >/dev/null
491	+  # Every file the manifest lists for the skill, as "<sha256>  <path>" lines.
492	+  want=$(jq -r --arg n "$s" '.skills[] | select(.name == $n) | .files[] | "\(.exactSha256)  \(.path)"' "$manifest")
493	+  [ -n "$want" ] || { fail "$s" "no entry in the manifest"; continue; }
494	+  if out=$(cd "$src" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$want" | sha256sum --quiet -c - 2>&1); then
495	+    pass "$s matches this build's manifest ($(printf '%s\n' "$want" | wc -l) files)"
496	+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
497	+done
498	+
499	+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
500	+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

524	# still evaluate?" check costs nothing on the laptop.
525	#
526	# Driven by `hmeval --ci` (home.nix), which commits the working tree — dirty or
527	# not — to an `eval/**` branch and reads the result back out of this job's log.
528	# The branch is throwaway and `hmeval` deletes it afterwards.
529	#
530	# This does NOT push to attic. nix-home.yml owns the closure cache; this job
531	# only answers a question, so a scratch eval cannot poison the cache with paths
532	# built from a commit that never reached master.
533	name: nix-eval
534	
535	on:

537	    branches: ["eval/**"]

539	
540	# Unlike nix-home.yml, this one cancels. A closure build that gets discarded
541	# wastes twenty minutes of work someone is waiting on; a superseded eval is
542	# just a stale answer, and `hmeval` is already watching the newer run.

544	  group: nix-eval-${{ github.ref }}

546	
547	jobs:
548	  eval:
549	    # Same runner and image as nix-home.yml, for the same reasons — see
550	    # docs/ci-nix-home.md before changing either. In particular: no `uses:`
551	    # steps (the image has no node), and no awk/sed/grep, which is why the
552	    # request file below is parsed in pure bash.
553	    runs-on: privileged
554	    container:
555	      image: nixos/nix@sha256:1a711b619c8a713eff32c3f8d8781b3b4d0130cb91c0a57f67e87abfeeb90b01
556	    env:
557	      NIX_CONFIG: |
558	        experimental-features = nix-command flakes
559	        netrc-file = /root/.config/nix/netrc
560	        extra-substituters = http://attic.attic.svc.cluster.local/kube
561	        extra-trusted-public-keys = kube:REDACTED
562	        max-jobs = 6
563	        cores = 4
564	        sandbox = true

567	      # userland. One rev for both, so a bump moves them together.
568	      TOOLS_REV: 29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299
569	      # Which host tests/ should believe it is running on; see the tests branch

574	        env:
575	          ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}

577	          set -eu
578	          mkdir -p /root/.config/nix
579	          umask 077
580	          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
581	            attic.attic.svc.cluster.local "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
582	            > /root/.config/nix/netrc
583	          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
584	            attic.ko.ag "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
585	            >> /root/.config/nix/netrc

605	      # below. Keep them in step: hmeval slices the job log between them, so a
606	      # renamed marker silently turns every run into "no output".

608	        env:
609	          # Load-bearing, and not obviously so. The credential helper configured
610	          # in the previous step answers out of $FORGE_TOKEN *at the moment nix
611	          # shells out to git*, which is here — so a helper installed globally
612	          # but an env set only on the earlier step leaves this one answering
613	          # with an empty password. The failure is not an auth error either; it
614	          # surfaces as `error: Failed to fetch git repository
615	          # 'https://forge.ko.ag/sauyon/dotfiles-private.git'` partway down a
616	          # stack trace about home.activation, which reads like a broken config.
617	          # nix-home.yml sets it on its build step for exactly this reason.
618	          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}
619	        run: |
620	          set -eu
621	
622	          req=.hmeval-request
623	          if [ ! -f "$req" ]; then
624	            echo "no $req in this commit — nothing to run."
625	            echo "This workflow is driven by \`hmeval --ci\`; pushing an eval/**"
626	            echo "branch by hand does not carry a request."
627	            exit 1
628	          fi
629	
630	          # Pure bash: no awk/sed/grep in this image. Values are single-line by
631	          # construction (hmeval rejects newlines before it writes the file).
632	          mode=; hosts=; tests=; attr=
633	          while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
634	            case "$k" in
635	              mode)  mode=$v ;;
636	              hosts) hosts=$v ;;
637	              tests) tests=$v ;;
638	              attr)  attr=$v ;;
639	            esac
640	          done < "$req"

642	          echo "hmeval: mode=$mode"
643	          echo "---8<--- hmeval"
644	          rc=0
645	
646	          # $hosts and $tests are unquoted in the loops below ON PURPOSE: they
647	          # are space-separated lists and the word splitting is the mechanism.
648	          # Quoting them turns the whole list into one argument, which fails as
649	          # "attribute 'utsuho fujiwara ...' missing" rather than as a syntax
650	          # error, so it looks like a broken flake instead of a broken quote.
651	          # hmeval guarantees they contain no other whitespace.
652	
653	          case "$mode" in
654	            eval)
655	              # --no-link/--raw keeps this to evaluation plus whatever IFD the
656	              # config genuinely needs; nothing is pushed anywhere.
657	              for h in $hosts; do
658	                if out=$(nix eval --raw ".#homeConfigurations.$h.activationPackage.drvPath"); then
659	                  printf '  %-10s %s\n' "$h" "$out"
660	                else
661	                  printf '  %-10s FAILED\n' "$h"
662	                  rc=1
663	                fi
664	              done
665	              ;;
666	            attr)
667	              if out=$(nix eval --raw ".#$attr"); then
668	                printf '  %s\n' "$out"
669	              else
670	                printf '  FAILED: .#%s\n' "$attr"
671	                rc=1
672	              fi
673	              ;;
674	            tests)
675	              # Several scripts in tests/ build the thing they test by way of
676	              # `homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname)` — fine on a box that
677	              # is one of the hosts, useless in a container whose hostname is
678	              # its own ID. Run 137 died twice over with
679	              #
680	              #   does not provide attribute
681	              #   'homeConfigurations.328998cea6c4.config.home.packages'
682	              #
683	              # Rather than teach eight scripts a new seam, tell the ephemeral
684	              # container it is a host. It only ever needs to be *a* host whose
685	              # config contains the script under test; utsuho has all of them.
686	              printf '%s' "$TEST_HOST" > /etc/hostname
687	              echo "  (as $TEST_HOST)"
688	
689	              # tests/*.sh are ordinary shell: they want coreutils, grep, sed
690	              # and jq, none of which the nix image has. Run them inside a
691	              # pinned shell rather than teaching each script to cope.
692	              tools="github:NixOS/nixpkgs/$TOOLS_REV"

694	                echo "  === $t"
695	                if nix shell \
696	                     "$tools#bash" "$tools#coreutils" "$tools#gnugrep" \
697	                     "$tools#gnused" "$tools#gawk" "$tools#git" \
698	                     "$tools#jq" "$tools#diffutils" \
699	                     -c bash "$t"; then
700	                  echo "  === $t PASSED"
701	                else
702	                  echo "  === $t FAILED"
703	                  rc=1
704	                fi
705	              done
706	              ;;
707	            *)
708	              echo "  unknown mode: $mode"
709	              rc=1
710	              ;;
711	          esac
712	
713	          echo "---8<--- end"
714	          exit $rc

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal, and that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this
+# Orca build expects. Also its launchers: node mode, signals forwarded into
+# the sandbox (so `orca-ide serve` stops cleanly), Ctrl-C, and a GUI that
+# outlives `orca-ide open`.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
+# against the host's libraries outside the FHS env. The skills are stubs
+# that tell the agent to run `orca-ide skills get <name>`, so a skill without a
+# working CLI is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a commit separately
+# from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other silently installs
+# guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes in
+# resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }

+# not bind it in, so fall back to uname -n there.
+HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || uname -n).config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
+}

+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }

+# outlives that parent, and the GUI's bwrap is the launcher's child, so

+  pass "skills rev ${rev:0:8} is this build's sourceCommit"

+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }

+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)

+    pass "$s matches this build's manifest ($(printf '%s\n' "$want" | wc -l) files)"
+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
+done

+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

# Ad-hoc evaluation and test runs on the in-cluster runner, so a "does this
# still evaluate?" check costs nothing on the laptop.
#
# Driven by `hmeval --ci` (home.nix), which commits the working tree — dirty or
# not — to an `eval/**` branch and reads the result back out of this job's log.
# The branch is throwaway and `hmeval` deletes it afterwards.
#
# This does NOT push to attic. nix-home.yml owns the closure cache; this job
# only answers a question, so a scratch eval cannot poison the cache with paths
# built from a commit that never reached master.
name: nix-eval

on:
  push:
    branches: ["eval/**"]
  workflow_dispatch:

# Unlike nix-home.yml, this one cancels. A closure build that gets discarded
# wastes twenty minutes of work someone is waiting on; a superseded eval is
# just a stale answer, and `hmeval` is already watching the newer run.
concurrency:
  group: nix-eval-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  eval:
    # Same runner and image as nix-home.yml, for the same reasons — see
    # docs/ci-nix-home.md before changing either. In particular: no `uses:`
    # steps (the image has no node), and no awk/sed/grep, which is why the
    # request file below is parsed in pure bash.
    runs-on: privileged
    container:
      image: nixos/nix@sha256:1a711b619c8a713eff32c3f8d8781b3b4d0130cb91c0a57f67e87abfeeb90b01
    env:
      NIX_CONFIG: |
        experimental-features = nix-command flakes
        netrc-file = /root/.config/nix/netrc
        extra-substituters = http://attic.attic.svc.cluster.local/kube
        extra-trusted-public-keys = kube:REDACTED
        max-jobs = 6
        cores = 4
        sandbox = true
      # Pinned the same way nix-home.yml pins its attic-client: the image ships
      # no coreutils/grep/jq, and the test scripts in tests/ assume a normal
      # userland. One rev for both, so a bump moves them together.
      TOOLS_REV: 29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299
      # Which host tests/ should believe it is running on; see the tests branch
      # below. Any host with a full desktop config will do.
      TEST_HOST: utsuho
    steps:
      - name: authorise nix against attic
        env:
          ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          mkdir -p /root/.config/nix
          umask 077
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.attic.svc.cluster.local "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            > /root/.config/nix/netrc
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.ko.ag "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            >> /root/.config/nix/netrc

      - name: checkout
        run: |
          set -eu
          git clone https://forge.ko.ag/${{ github.repository }}.git .
          git checkout --detach ${{ github.sha }}
          git --no-pager log -1 --oneline

      # Do NOT echo $FORGE_TOKEN or enable `set -x` here.
      - name: authorise git against the private input
        env:
          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          git config --global credential."https://forge.ko.ag".username oauth2
          git config --global credential."https://forge.ko.ag".helper \
            '!f() { test "$1" = get && printf "password=%s\n" "$FORGE_TOKEN"; }; f'

      # The whole contract with `hmeval` is this file plus the two markers
      # below. Keep them in step: hmeval slices the job log between them, so a
      # renamed marker silently turns every run into "no output".
      - name: run the request
        env:
          # Load-bearing, and not obviously so. The credential helper configured
          # in the previous step answers out of $FORGE_TOKEN *at the moment nix
          # shells out to git*, which is here — so a helper installed globally
          # but an env set only on the earlier step leaves this one answering
          # with an empty password. The failure is not an auth error either; it
          # surfaces as `error: Failed to fetch git repository
          # 'https://forge.ko.ag/sauyon/dotfiles-private.git'` partway down a
          # stack trace about home.activation, which reads like a broken config.
          # nix-home.yml sets it on its build step for exactly this reason.
          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu

          req=.hmeval-request
          if [ ! -f "$req" ]; then
            echo "no $req in this commit — nothing to run."
            echo "This workflow is driven by \`hmeval --ci\`; pushing an eval/**"
            echo "branch by hand does not carry a request."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Pure bash: no awk/sed/grep in this image. Values are single-line by
          # construction (hmeval rejects newlines before it writes the file).
          mode=; hosts=; tests=; attr=
          while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
            case "$k" in
              mode)  mode=$v ;;
              hosts) hosts=$v ;;
              tests) tests=$v ;;
              attr)  attr=$v ;;
            esac
          done < "$req"

          echo "hmeval: mode=$mode"
          echo "---8<--- hmeval"
          rc=0

          # $hosts and $tests are unquoted in the loops below ON PURPOSE: they
          # are space-separated lists and the word splitting is the mechanism.
          # Quoting them turns the whole list into one argument, which fails as
          # "attribute 'utsuho fujiwara ...' missing" rather than as a syntax
          # error, so it looks like a broken flake instead of a broken quote.
          # hmeval guarantees they contain no other whitespace.

          case "$mode" in
            eval)
              # --no-link/--raw keeps this to evaluation plus whatever IFD the
              # config genuinely needs; nothing is pushed anywhere.
              for h in $hosts; do
                if out=$(nix eval --raw ".#homeConfigurations.$h.activationPackage.drvPath"); then
                  printf '  %-10s %s\n' "$h" "$out"
                else
                  printf '  %-10s FAILED\n' "$h"
                  rc=1
                fi
              done
              ;;
            attr)
              if out=$(nix eval --raw ".#$attr"); then
                printf '  %s\n' "$out"
              else
                printf '  FAILED: .#%s\n' "$attr"
                rc=1
              fi
              ;;
            tests)
              # Several scripts in tests/ build the thing they test by way of
              # `homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname)` — fine on a box that
              # is one of the hosts, useless in a container whose hostname is
              # its own ID. Run 137 died twice over with
              #
              #   does not provide attribute
              #   'homeConfigurations.328998cea6c4.config.home.packages'
              #
              # Rather than teach eight scripts a new seam, tell the ephemeral
              # container it is a host. It only ever needs to be *a* host whose
              # config contains the script under test; utsuho has all of them.
              printf '%s' "$TEST_HOST" > /etc/hostname
              echo "  (as $TEST_HOST)"

              # tests/*.sh are ordinary shell: they want coreutils, grep, sed
              # and jq, none of which the nix image has. Run them inside a
              # pinned shell rather than teaching each script to cope.
              tools="github:NixOS/nixpkgs/$TOOLS_REV"
              for t in $tests; do
                echo "  === $t"
                if nix shell \
                     "$tools#bash" "$tools#coreutils" "$tools#gnugrep" \
                     "$tools#gnused" "$tools#gawk" "$tools#git" \
                     "$tools#jq" "$tools#diffutils" \
                     -c bash "$t"; then
                  echo "  === $t PASSED"
                else
                  echo "  === $t FAILED"
                  rc=1
                fi
              done
              ;;
            *)
              echo "  unknown mode: $mode"
              rc=1
              ;;
          esac

          echo "---8<--- end"
          exit $rc

Round 7 review of `git diff origin/master..HEAD` (orca.nix, tests/orca-cli-skills.sh, tests/sandbox-fonts.sh). I made no changes.

**Critical:** none.

**Important (1):**

1. **The test calls `setsid`, which CI almost certainly doesn't have. Five cases would fail there.** (tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:95, :193)
   - CI runs the test inside `nix shell` with bash, coreutils, gnugrep, gnused, gawk, git, jq and diffutils (.forgejo/workflows/nix-eval.yml:695-699). `setsid` comes from util-linux, which is not on that list.
   - The image is the bare nixos/nix one. The workflow itself says it has no coreutils, grep or awk. The repo already assumes util-linux is missing in CI: tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:76 skips its case with "util-linux script(1) not available".
   - What breaks in CI:
     - `payload()` runs `env ... setsid ...`, which fails at once, so "ready" never appears and each payload wastes its 30s wait.
     - That fails four cases: "bwrap ignores HUP, INT and TERM", TERM forwarding, INT forwarding and group TERM.
     - The `bash -c 'setsid ...'` "GUI outlives the parent" case (it has used setsid since round 5) fails after 15s.
   - The round-6 commit only says the suite passed locally, with and without a pty. Nothing in the log shows a CI run since setsid was added.
   - I couldn't inspect the pinned image offline, so this is high-confidence rather than proven. One `hmeval --ci` tests run would settle it.
   - Fix options:
     - Add `"$tools#util-linux"` to the workflow's `nix shell` list.
     - Or have the test build its own util-linux from the flake's nixpkgs.
     - Or skip these cases when `command -v setsid` fails, the way the python3 case does. That loses CI coverage of the main claim, so adding util-linux is the better fix.

**Nits (2):**

1. **orca.nix:45** — the comment "Over 128 is a trap interrupting wait, or the child's own signal death" leaves out the third case the code handles: a plain exit over 128 (e.g. 148). The header comment (around line 18) covers it, but this inline comment is now incomplete.
2. **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:126** — "TERM to the whole group (a terminal's HUP, a control-group stop)". A terminal hangup sends HUP, not TERM, and no case sends HUP to the whole group. Something like "(a control-group stop; a terminal hangup is the same with HUP)" would be accurate.

**Checked and fine:**
- **Comments match the code.** Each orca.nix comment checks out against the current code:
  - The stat field indices (pgrp is `st[2]`, tpgid is `st[5]`), and the greedy `##*) ` handles parentheses in comm.
  - The dispositions: HUP, INT and TERM ignored, QUIT reset. `<&0` undoes the /dev/null stdin.
  - The re-raise list 129/130/143.
  - "Without a pid namespace (buildFHSEnv's default)": nixpkgs has `unsharePid ? false`, and `--die-with-parent` is on by default.
  - The Chromium and Node claims: Chromium's SetupSignalHandlers resets HUP, INT and TERM, and Node resets inherited dispositions.
  - nixGL's wrappers `exec` all the way down, so `$w`'s child really is bwrap. That holds up the SigIgn case.
  - In the test, the "setsid execs in place" note is right for a non-interactive shell, whose background jobs don't lead their own group. The `--default-signal=INT` reasoning is right too.
- **Each case fails on its regression:**
  - Removing `--ignore-signal` fails SigIgn, group TERM and Ctrl-C.
  - Removing forwarding fails TERM and INT.
  - Removing the foreground check gives `ints=2`.
  - Re-raising every status over 128 makes the exit-148 case stop on TSTP and come back as 124 from timeout.
  - A plain exec in the GUI launcher fails "GUI outlives".
- **With and without a controlling tty:** the payloads run under setsid, so they have no terminal either way. The pty case brings its own tty and is skipped without python3. The node-mode, exit-148 and stdin cases don't depend on the tty.
- **CI's bash has `compgen`:** pinned TOOLS_REV `#bash` evaluates to `bash-interactive-5.3p9`, so `outside()` works. (The non-interactive nixpkgs bash has no `compgen`, but CI doesn't use it.)
- **Secrets:** the test prints no env values. `outside()` passes only ORCA_* variable names to `env -u`. Payloads print fixed strings. Failure messages show only CLI output (produced with ORCA_* removed from the env) or Node stderr. There's no `set -x`. The diff adds no emails or private data.
- **Cleanup:** an EXIT trap removes `$T`. Every `payload` is killed and waited on. Detached payloads (the GUI-lifetime one and the pty child) exit on their own within 4s and 20s. Nothing kills by pattern.
- **Security:** nothing found. Heredocs are quoted, store paths are interpolated at build time, and the skills are read-only store symlinks with a pinned rev and hash.
- **tests/sandbox-fonts.sh:** both edits are correct (the `orca-ide-app` rename and the `uname -n` fallback).

I didn't re-raise the nits earlier rounds left on purpose: the signal-before-fork window, traps set after `&`, and the duplicated skill list.
